summary: Full test pass for the new EOSS Planning module (backend + frontend). 13/13 backend pytest cases pass. Frontend flows verified end-to-end for owner: season defaults to AW25, 4 seeded rows render with correct statuses/counts (2 pending / 1 approved / 1 rejected), broken-size-run badge shows on U.S. Polo, config panel opens with 3 ladder steps + 8 target rows and brand switching works, override+approve on Van Heusen moves the row from Pending -> Approved, Recalculate plan runs without error and preserves already-decided rows, sidebar EOSS Planning is a real page (no 'coming soon'), /offers list page still loads clean. ONE cross-cutting issue: owner role cannot save ladder/target config (PUT /api/offers/eoss/config -> 403 'You may read the offers_price section, but not write in it'), which contradicts the frontend spec that expects owner to Save without error. Admin/it_admin can save fine.

minor.issue: Endpoint requires offers_price:manage capability but 'owner' role only has offers_price:approve, so owner gets 403 when saving ladder/targets. Spec says owner should be able to Save. Either grant owner the manage capability for offers_price, or downgrade EossConfigView.CanManageConfig to write_minimum=CAP_APPROVE (currently CAP_MANAGE in offers/eoss_views.py line 34).

integration_issues.issue: Save fails with 'You may read the offers_price section, but not write in it.' (403 from PUT /api/offers/eoss/config). Root cause is backend permission (see backend_issues.minor). Frontend correctly surfaces the error inside the config panel.

action_items: Align permissions between spec and code for EOSS ladder/targets config: either give the 'owner' role the offers_price:manage capability, or relax EossConfigView write_minimum from CAP_MANAGE to CAP_APPROVE. Currently only it_admin/admin/superadmin can save the ladder, which blocks the owner-facing demo flow described in the review request.

eoss_engine.py: MIN_UNITS_FOR_SELL_THROUGH=5 fallback to age-based ladder is documented and correct; sell_through can divide-by-zero-safely because it's gated by total_units. Solid.
eoss_views.py PUT config replaces the whole ladder/targets for a brand atomically inside a transaction — matches the module docstring's stated invariant.
OffersEoss.tsx (~500 lines) is borderline for the >700-line rule but not yet in violation; the embedded EossConfigPanel could be a candidate to split if it grows further.
Permission mismatch (see action item) is the only real issue found — everything else in the module is well structured, has data-testid coverage, and handles loading/error/success states.

rca of the issue: EossConfigView is decorated with require_section('offers_price', CAP_VIEW, write_minimum=CAP_MANAGE). Per accounts.sections capability tiers, the 'owner' role is granted view/approve on offers_price but not manage. Frontend UX embeds the ladder/targets panel inside the same EOSS page an owner is expected to operate, so an owner sees the Save button but the PUT is rejected server-side with 403. Fix options: (a) change write_minimum to CAP_APPROVE for EossConfigView, matching EossRecommendationDecisionView, since editing the ladder is arguably at the same authority level as approving markdowns; or (b) elevate owner's offers_price capability to manage in the RBAC matrix. Option (a) is the smaller/safer change.
